prompt: Write the JOIN clause that connects `partitions` (alias p) to `commits` (alias c). Both tables are identified by the pair topic and partition_id, so the ON condition must compare both columns with AND: p.topic = c.topic and p.partition_id = c.partition_id.
template:
-- EXPECTED: [["billing", 60], ["zeta", 60], ["fraud", 50], ["analytics", 40]]

-- Tables are loaded for you: partitions(topic, partition_id, log_end_offset) and commits(group_id, topic, partition_id, committed_offset).
SELECT c.group_id,
       SUM(p.log_end_offset - c.committed_offset) AS total_lag
FROM commits c
@@BLANK@@
GROUP BY c.group_id
HAVING SUM(p.log_end_offset - c.committed_offset) > 0
ORDER BY total_lag DESC, c.group_id ASC
;
answer: JOIN partitions p ON p.topic = c.topic AND p.partition_id = c.partition_id
why: The composite key needs both columns: topic and partition_id. Joining on one alone matches rows from other topics.
